vulnerability_patterns.description: A devm_kasprintf() result may be NULL on allocation failure. Pre-patch code immediately stored that possibly NULL pointer into aux_driver->name or aux_dev->name and continued initialization, allowing later code paths to consume the name field as a valid string/object identifier. The patch blocks this by checking if (!name) and returning -ENOMEM before the field assignment.
trigger_conditions: A local variable is initialized or assigned from devm_kasprintf(...)
The returned pointer is not checked for NULL before first consumption
The unchecked pointer is assigned into a struct field such as aux_driver->name or aux_dev->name
The function continues normal initialization after the assignment rather than returning on allocation failure
fix_patterns: Return an error such as -ENOMEM before assigning the possibly NULL pointer into aux_driver->name or aux_dev->name
Use the NULL guard as a barrier between the allocation result and subsequent object initialization

suggestions: First-draft detector should anchor on devm_kasprintf(...) assigned to a local variable named or used as name, followed by assignment of that variable into a struct field before any if (!var) or equivalent NULL check.
Do not require proof of the eventual dereference in the first draft; the patch-local sink is the unchecked propagation into aux_driver->name or aux_dev->name and continued initialization.
Treat the newly added if (!name) return -ENOMEM as the barrier, but do not make the exact error code a hard requirement except as a secondary precision filter.
Local AST plus intra-procedural CFG/def-use is sufficient for the patch-local pattern; cross-file analysis is not needed unless later refining for downstream users of the name field.
Use field names ending in .name and nullable kernel allocation/formatting helpers such as devm_kasprintf as useful secondary filters, not as the only match condition.

analysis_rationale: The patch adds immediate NULL guards after two devm_kasprintf() calls in drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c. Before the patch, the returned name pointer was consumed by assigning it into aux_driver->name or aux_dev->name and execution continued. The concrete fix-shape is an allocation/formatting helper that may return NULL followed by early return -ENOMEM before the value is stored into object name fields and later initialization proceeds.
